subject: Learning Methods
title: Targeted Memory Reactivation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Targeted Memory Reactivation usable.

hook.text: Students who smelled roses while studying and again during sleep remembered the material 13 % better.

buildup.text: Targeted memory reactivation uses sensory cues during sleep to reactivate memories and boost their consolidation.

discovery.text: Sound cues work too. Playing a tone associated with specific learning during deep sleep strengthens those memories.

twist.text: The cues must be subtle enough not to wake you. And they only work during deep sleep, not REM or light sleep stages.

climax.text: This technique is still mostly experimental. But studying with a consistent scent and using it during sleep may enhance.

punchline.text: Same scent while learning and sleeping. Memory gets a boost.

quiz.question: During which sleep stage do targeted memory reactivation cues work?
